title: Toasted Coconut Steel-Cut Oatmeal
changes_from_base: Butter-toasted steel-cut oats simmer in water and coconut milk instead of cow's milk, then get toasted coconut flakes and light brown sugar stirred through.
summary: Creaminess from tinged coconut milk and toasted coconut flakes enriches these steel-cut oats, creating a breakfast that tastes indulgent yet remains straightforward to make.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast coconut
steps.text: Toast 30 g unsweetened coconut flakes in a small dry pan over medium-low 2-3 min, stirring, until golden; tip onto a plate.

steps.title: Toast oats
steps.text: Melt 14 g butter in a large saucepan over medium heat, add 175 g steel-cut oats and toast about 2 min, stirring, until golden.

steps.title: Liquid
steps.text: Pour in 720 ml water and 240 ml tinned coconut milk, bring to the boil.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Simmer gently over medium-low about 20 min, stirring now and then, until creamy but chewy.

steps.title: Rest and finish
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in ¼ tsp salt, cover, rest 5 min, then stir in toasted coconut and 38 g light brown sugar; season to taste with more salt if needed.

tips: Toast coconut flakes first so they stay crisp; add them after cooking to prevent burning.
Tinned coconut milk adds richness; give it a good shake before opening.
Watch the oats while simmering and stir occasionally to prevent sticking on the bottom.
storage: Serve hot; leftover porridge keeps in the fridge for 2 days and reheats gently over low heat with a splash of water or milk. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
